diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, we ask what the largest possible set of measures  \(\mathrm{F}\) is that any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for.

If we drop this and allow \emph{fully $y_\star$–dependent} affine maps $L_{y_\star}(x,y)=A(y_\star)x+B(y_\star)y+c(y_\star)$, the situation changes: one can engineer many non-Gaussian $\pi$ with exact affine transports that lie strictly beyond $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$.
Clearly $\pi$ is not in $\mathrm{F}$ for general $f$ and has the exact affine conditioning map $L_{y_\star}(x,y) = f(y_\star)y$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract describes F as 'the largest possible set of measures that any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for' and concludes that 'among affine transports, the EnKU is near-optimal'. In the paper, F is defined only as the union of exact sets over weakly y_star-dependent affine conditioning maps, L(x,y) = A(pi)x + B(pi)y + c(pi,y_star), with A(pi), B(pi) independent of y_star (intro and Equation eq:weakly_y_star), and Theorem thm:F_char proves optimality only within that restricted class. The paper's own Section 3.2 shows that dropping the restriction yields exact fully y_star-dependent affine maps for non-Gaussian measures 'strictly beyond E^EnKU' and outside F. So the abstract's unqualified optimality claim asserts more than the formal content supports.

failure_location.quote: Thus, among  affine transports, the EnKU is near-optimal for exact distributional conditioning beyond the Gaussian setting.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the qualifier 'weakly y_star-dependent' into the abstract's definition of F and into the concluding optimality sentence, matching the body's precise scope.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee 'among affine transports the EnKU is near-optimal' is materially misleading: it holds only among weakly y_star-dependent affine maps; fully y_star-dependent affine maps (Section 3.2) achieve exactness strictly beyond F.
issues.title: Abstract overstates F and EnKU optimality to all affine transports
issues.why_classification: A local wording repair adding the restriction already established in the body preserves every formal result, guarantee, and rate; no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To rule out spurious constant offsets in the constant \(c\), we assume \(\Sigma_{YY}\) is invertible.
Further, it is the unique affine update achieving exact conditioning for any measure in $\mathrm{F}$ except for a subclass of strongly symmetric distributions.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts uniqueness of the exact affine map for every symmetry-free pi in E^EnKU. Theorem thm:enkf_update_unique alone yields only necessary spectral conditions (rho(A) <= 1, BP_Y = -A Sigma_XY Sigma_YY^dagger P_Y, no unit eigenvalue different from 1); uniqueness as a map follows only from Corollary cor:enkf_char, which additionally assumes Cov(Y) invertible. If Cov(Y) is singular while nu has non-singular covariance and pi avoids all three symmetry classes, any B differing from -K by a matrix vanishing on Im(Cov(Y)) (with c adjusted) gives a different affine map whose pushforward of pi still equals the posterior, so the unqualified uniqueness claim is false as stated.

failure_location.quote: In Theorem \ref{thm:enkf_update_unique} we answer the second question: excluding strongly symmetric distributions, given $\pi \in \mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU}$, $y_\star \in \R^m$ the EnKU update $L_{\pi, y_\star}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$ is the \emph{only} affine map  that is exact for $\pi$ at $y_\star$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the qualifier 'with non-singular Cov(Y)' to the uniqueness statements in the introduction and abstract.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory uniqueness guarantee (and the parallel abstract sentence 'it is the unique affine update achieving exact conditioning for any measure in F except for a subclass of strongly symmetric distributions') overclaims: uniqueness holds only under non-singular Sigma_YY, a hypothesis Corollary cor:enkf_char makes explicit but the summaries omit.
issues.title: Intro uniqueness claim omits the non-singular Cov(Y) hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The precise formal statements (Theorem, Corollary) are correct; restoring the already-stated invertibility condition in two summary sentences is a short local fix preserving all substantive guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a simple consequence of the fact that $X + BY$ is Gaussian and there is an affine transport map between any two non-singular Gaussians.

issues.failure_explanation: For Gaussian pi with X = Z + MY (Z independent of Y), exactness of l(x,y)=Ax+By+c at y_star forces the covariance identity A Cov(Z) A^T + (AM+B) Cov(Y) (AM+B)^T = Cov(Z), so B cannot be prescribed arbitrarily. Scalar counterexample: Z, Y i.i.d. N(0,1), X = Z + Y (M = 1); exactness at any y_star requires a^2 + (a+b)^2 = 1, i.e. 2a^2 + 4a + 3 = 0 for b = 2, which has no real solution, while Cov(X + 2Y) = Var(Z + 3Y) = 5 is full rank. The paper's own composition argument only yields maps of the form T(x + By), whose Y-coefficient is the transport's linear part times B, not B itself, so the cited reasoning does not establish the universal claim.

failure_location.quote: for every choice of $B$ (assuming $\Cov(X+BY)$ has full rank for all $y_\star$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim by the correct statement proven by the transport composition (exact affine maps exist for a constrained set of Y-gains, e.g. B with (AM+B)Cov(Y)(AM+B)^T preponderance-compatible), or exhibit the genuine free-parameter family.
issues.overall_effect: Only the motivational example is affected; no labelled theorem, proposition, or algorithm relies on the false parameterization.
issues.title: False claim that any Y-gain B admits an exact affine map for Gaussians
issues.why_classification: A one-to-two-line correction of an unlabelled introductory sentence; all theorems, guarantees, and the non-uniqueness message for Gaussians survive unchanged.
